subject: zoology

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.62, VSAQ 166). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK DIFFERENCE: the book prints the human optimum as 98.4°F (or) 37°C. 37°C is exactly 98.6°F, and 98.6°F is the standard value, so this card writes 37°C first with 98.6°F beside it; a paper that expects 98.4°F still accepts 37°C.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Optimum temperature is the temperature at
which the metabolic activities of an
organism take place at their greatest level.
Above it and below it the rate of these
steps.why: The word optimum means best, not highest, so the second line — the rate falls on BOTH sides — is what stops the answer from being read as the maximum temperature the animal can stand.
common_mistakes: Writing that it is the highest temperature the animal can survive. That is the maximum, not the optimum.
Leaving out the word metabolic. The definition is about the rate of metabolic activity.
steps.memory_tip: Optimum is the peak of a hill: the rate falls whether you go up or down from it.
steps.margin_note: One sentence for the definition and one line saying the rate falls on both sides.

steps.label: Value in man
lines: The optimum temperature of the human body is
Each species has its own optimum
steps.why: A named number turns a general definition into a checkable answer, and the human body temperature is the one value in the syllabus every student already knows.
common_mistakes: Writing 37°F. The value is 37 degrees CELSIUS.
Writing that every animal has the same optimum. Each species has its own.
steps.memory_tip: 37 in Celsius, about 98.6 in Fahrenheit — one body, two scales.
steps.margin_note: Give the number with its unit. One extra line that the value differs between species.

insider_note: Give the number: a definition with no value attached usually scores one of the two marks.
